explainer.lead: NeurIPS is the Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, one of the premier annual AI/ML research conferences alongside ICML and ICLR. It is a primary venue where high-impact machine learning research is presented.

tiers.eli5: It is one of the big yearly gatherings where AI researchers show each other their newest work, like a major trade fair for machine learning ideas.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers target NeurIPS to publish refereed papers and to follow the invited talks and posters that define current directions. A practical point: it is held annually in December and includes workshop and competition days after the main programme.
tiers.paperLevel: An annual machine learning and computational neuroscience conference, first held in 1987, with three days of invited talks plus oral and poster presentations, followed by two days of workshops and competitions. Known limit: it is one venue among several peer conferences, not a formal standard.

explainer.example: A team submits a paper on a new training method, presents it as a poster at the December meeting, and later discusses it at a two-day workshop.
